title: Snake-3D: Differentiable Learning for Cross-Tier Logic Path Snaking Optimization in 3D ICs
problem: 3D IC designs suffer from excessive snaking along critical paths and require many bond pads, complicating production and degrading timing.
motivation: Post-Moore 3D ICs offer superior timing and lower power but current flows rely on bin-based FM partitioning that overlooks inter-bin connections.
method: It divides a 3D circuit into functional sections (partitioning) using gradient-based optimization (calculating the best partition by following slopes of errors), running on GPU with PyTorch. The cost function accounts for snaking — the winding paths signals take through layers — and timing constraints (how quickly signals must travel). It also spaces circuit elements evenly to avoid clustering. This early-stage optimization reduces wasteful winding on speed-critical paths and cuts the number of bond pads (metal connections between layers) needed.
key_novelty: It combines snaking and timing awareness into gradient-based partitioning at the earliest design stage, accelerated on GPU.
contributions: 29% reduction in final bond pad count
47% bond pad reduction vs GNN-based methods

metrics.speedup: 7.4x faster than GNN-based, similar to default flow

limitations: Evaluated on limited technology nodes (7nm and 28nm); applicability to other nodes unclear.
